title: Annie: Hard-Knock Morning
description: A laundry basket escape, a stray mutt, and a mansion that isn't an orphanage—Go Deep into one Broadway morning that changes everything.
imageHint: Red curls, a hard-knock chorus, and a city that might say yes

questions.question: In the orphanage, Annie and the girls scrub floors while singing which bitter anthem about chores and Miss Hannigan?
questions.explanation: Buckets, brushes, and a choreography of resentment. The sun will come out later—first they have to survive the morning.

questions.question: After that hard-knock chorus, Annie escapes and comforts herself with the promise that "the sun'll come out" in which song?
acceptedAnswers: the sun will come out tomorrow
choices: I Don't Need Anything But You
questions.explanation: Lyricist Martin Charnin bought a Little Orphan Annie book as a Christmas gift, read it instead of wrapping it, and chased the rights. The friend never got the book.

questions.question: Annie sings Tomorrow to a stray mutt running from the dogcatcher, then names him on the spot. What is his name?
questions.explanation: The original Broadway Sandy was a shelter mutt found by apprentice William Berloni. That dog never missed a performance.

questions.question: Annie and Sandy end up leaving the hard-knock life for the Manhattan mansion of which billionaire?
questions.explanation: A two-week trial stay turns into a found family. The decoys are all from the show: radio host, con-man brother, laundry man.

questions.question: Warbucks later takes Annie to the White House, where which president and his cabinet learn to sing Tomorrow?
questions.explanation: In the musical, her optimism nudges FDR toward New Deal hope. Earlier, a shantytown sings a sarcastic thank-you to Hoover. Leapin' lizards stays mostly in the comic strip.

easterEgg.title: Before Carrie Bradshaw
easterEgg.text: Sarah Jessica Parker took over the title role during the original Broadway run. Molly Ringwald and Alyssa Milano both played orphans in the show, and Jane Lynch made her Broadway debut as Miss Hannigan.
